newsitem.title: USA: CPC to spin off corn refining business.
newsitem.headline: CPC to spin off corn refining business.

text.p: CPC International Inc Wednesday said it plans to spin off its corn refining business to CPC shareholders as a new independent publicly-owned company.

The new company, with businesses in 18 countries, will comprise CPC's corn refining operations in the United States, Canada, Latin America, Asia, and Africa; its interest in a joint venture in Mexico; and other joint venture interests, as well as licensing and technical agreements, chiefly in Asia and Africa. The sales of these operations, excluding the sales of non-consolidated joint ventures, were $1.5 billion in 1996.

The objective of the spin-off, said C.R. Shoemate, CPC's chairman and chief executive, is "to give both CPC and the new corn refining company the focus, flexibility, and resources they need for faster growth of sales, volumes, and profits."

After a spin-off, CPC International will be a global branded packaged food company consisting of its existing businesses in branded grocery products, baking, and foodservice. CPC's branded grocery products and foodservice businesses market products including Hellmann's and Best Foods mayonnaise, Knorr soups, sauces, and bouillons, Mazola corn oil, and Skippy peanut butter.
Konrad Schlatter, currently senior vice president and chief financial officer of CPC International, will be chairman and chief executive officer of the new corn refining company.
Samuel Scott will continue as president and chief operating officer of the new company and will be responsible for the day-to-day operations of the business.

CPC does not expect to assign any of its existing debt to the new company. The deal is expected to be in the form of a distribution of the shares of the new company and may be preceded by an initial public offering of stock in the new company. It is subject to approval of a definitive plan by CPC's board and receipt of a ruling by the IRS that the deal will be tax-free to CPC and shareholders.
The transaction is expected to be completed by year end.

CPC's baking business makes and markets Thomas' English muffins and bagels; Entenmann's sweet baked products; Freihofer's, Oroweat, and Arnold breads and rolls; Boboli pizza crusts; and other premium fresh baked products.

CPC is the third largest corn refining company worldwide, including its partnerships around the world. It is the global leader in dextrose, a high value-added corn refining product, and in corn starch.
